text.p: These are the major headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Ottawa eyes crime prevention: Proposed C$30-million program would try to divert youths from criminal path.
- Firm hired to find megacity savings: Source says data to back arguments.
- Ottawa firm on salmon licences: Report due today puts B.C. in spot.
- Major's political fortunes go from bad to worse: Minister resigns, party divided, House majority in jeopardy.
- Bre-X losing grip on gold find: Indonesian government cancels licence applications to operate mine at Busang discovery.
- Stock markets tumble, again: TSE and Dow drop for second time in four days.
- Single EU market far from a reality: From chocolate to taxes to electrical plugs, member nations disagree over a host of details.
- Toronto real estate tycoon Murray Frum sells stake in malls: Deal with RioCan worth C$46-million.
- Power struggle traps Bre-X: Reports that Bre-X's applications to develop its huge gold find have been cancelled are linked to infighting in the Indonesian government.
